chunks: Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Harawi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Najda narrated to us, saying: Abu Bashr Khatn al-Muqarri narrated to us, saying: Mu'amr ibn Suleiman narrated to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

For every Prophet there is a special supplication which he has made and a request which he has asked for, but I have kept back my special supplication for my intercession for my nation on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's reserved supplication for intercession?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Khisal, Anas ibn Malik reports that while other Prophets utilized their unique supplication immediately upon receiving it, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) reserved his special prayer specifically for his intercession (shafa'ah) on the Day of Judgment. This distinction highlights the unique eschatological role of the Prophet in Shia theology, where his reserved supplication serves as a decisive means of salvation for his umma, underscoring the continuity of divine mercy through his prophetic authority.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-103 Abul Hassan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus narrated that Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Haravy quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Najda, on the authority of Abu Bashar Khatn al-Muqar’ri, on the authority of Mu’amir ibn Suleiman that he had heard Anas ibn Malik say that he had heard God’s Prophet (MGB) say,

“Each Prophet has a special supplication which he has said to God and in which he has asked God for something. However, I put off my special supplication to intercede on behalf of my nation on the Resurrection Day.”
